To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the new pseudopotential and basis set approach provides a highly accurate and computationally efficient way of describing the electronic structure of the 5 d transition metals, (2) the new pseudoptential and basis set combination can be used to accurately describe the electronic structure of transition metal complexes and molecules containing 5 d transition metal atoms, (3) the new pseudpotential and basis set combination is transferable and can be used to describe the electronic structure in a wide range of chemical systems

we have generated new relativistic pseudopotentials for Hf-Pt that reproduce all-electron energy data with an accuracy of approximately 0,01 eV for the valence energy spectrum and approximately 0,05 eV for the individual relativistic states, and that we have developed a series of correlation consistent valence basis sets for the new pseudopotential, which are calibrated by all-electron triple zeta quality correlation consistent valence sets.
we have developed energy-consistent pseudopotentails and correlation-consistent basis sets for the atoms Hf-Pt that are accurate to approximately 0.1 eV for the valence correlation energy.

the development of new relativistic energy-consis-tent pseudopotentials for the 5th row elements Hf-Pb and new correlation consistent basis sets to be used in conjunction with these pseudopotentials.
the generation of energy-consistent relativistic pseudopotentials for all the 5p and 5d transition elements.
the development of a new generation of pseudopotentials for the 5 d transition elements, Hf through Pt.

the new relativistic pseudopotentials are very accurate and can be used for the 5 d transition metals with confidence.
the present pseudopotentials are accurate enough for most purposes, and that the corresponding basis sets are well suited to describe the 5d metals in molecules.

the new pseudopotential and basis set combination provides a reliable and efficient tool for accurate quantum chemical studies of the 5 d transition metals.

the present pseudopotentials and associated basis sets are accurate to within 0.1 eV for the calculation of molecular energies and properties, and that the basis sets can be used to obtain accurate results for the relativistic energy levels of the 5s and 5p shells.

the new pseudopotential and basis sets are able to accurately reproduce the all-electronic reference data for the 5th row transition metals.
